dosageRegimens.notes: Start 50 mg daily; titrate at intervals of at least one week. Antidepressant effect takes 2-6 weeks; the interaction risks below start on day one.

indications.name: Panic disorder / OCD / PTSD / social anxiety disorder

dosageRegimens.notes: Panic and PTSD start lower, at 25 mg, because early activation is worse in anxiety disorders.

metabolismPathways.note: Weak to moderate inhibition. Enough to matter for triazolam, which has almost no margin.
Dose-dependent moderate inhibition — clinically slight at 50 mg, substantial at 150-200 mg. This single property drives most of sertraline's interactions in this database.

transporters.note: Weak. Relevant only where a P-gp substrate's safety depends on efflux, which in this set means loperamide.

activeMetabolites.name: N-desmethylsertraline
activeMetabolites.note: Roughly 20-fold less potent at SERT, so it contributes little to effect — but its half-life is 62-104 h against the parent's 26 h, so it dominates the washout period after stopping.

pharmacokinetics.notes: Steady state takes about a week. Enzyme inhibition builds over that period and decays over a longer one, because the desmethyl metabolite persists — so a sertraline interaction does not switch off the day the drug is stopped.

interactions.suggestedAction: A recognised combination that is sometimes deliberately prescribed, but it needs a prescriber who knows about both. Do not add one to the other without that, and watch for serotonin syndrome for the first two weeks and after every dose increase.
interactions.note: Additive serotonergic activity, plus additive cardiovascular effect. Sertraline also weakly inhibits CYP2D6, a minor amphetamine route.

interactions.suggestedAction: Avoid. If a cough suppressant is needed while on sertraline, use one without dextromethorphan — many combination cold products contain it unlabelled in the front-of-box name, so check the active ingredients panel.
interactions.note: The clearest serotonin syndrome risk in this database, and it is a double hit: sertraline inhibits CYP2D6, which is dextromethorphan's main clearance route, so parent levels rise several-fold at the same time as serotonergic tone rises. Cases are well documented at ordinary OTC doses.

interactions.suggestedAction: Treat a normal dextromethorphan dose as though it were several times larger.
interactions.note: CYP2D6 inhibition by sertraline converts an extensive metaboliser into a functional poor metaboliser. Recorded separately from the pharmacodynamic entry because the two need different mitigations: one is solved by dose, the other is not.

interactions.suggestedAction: Watch for agitation, raised blood pressure and insomnia, particularly in the first weeks of sertraline.
interactions.note: Weak additive serotonergic and sympathomimetic effect.

interactions.suggestedAction: Avoid regular combined use. If an NSAID is needed for more than a few days alongside an SSRI, gastroprotection with a PPI is the usual mitigation — esomeprazole and famotidine are both in this database for that reason.
interactions.note: SSRIs deplete platelet serotonin and impair platelet aggregation; NSAIDs damage the mucosa and inhibit platelet COX-1. Combined, upper GI bleeding risk rises several-fold above either alone. One of the most under-recognised pairings in ordinary outpatient use.

interactions.suggestedAction: Consider 25 mg daridorexant rather than 50 mg, particularly at sertraline doses of 150-200 mg.
interactions.note: Weak CYP3A4 inhibition against a substrate that is 89% dependent on that enzyme.

interactions.suggestedAction: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure closely, especially in the first weeks and after any sertraline increase. A propranolol dose reduction is often needed. Symptomatic bradycardia and heart block have been reported.
interactions.note: Moderate CYP2D6 inhibition by sertraline against a high-extraction CYP2D6 substrate. The effect scales with sertraline dose — slight at 50 mg, substantial at 200 mg — which means the interaction can appear weeks after both drugs were started.

interactions.suggestedAction: Expect more sedation than usual. Relevant if diphenhydramine is being used nightly for sleep.
interactions.note: Mutual CYP2D6 inhibition plus additive CNS effect.

interactions.suggestedAction: Separate the doses: at least 1 hour before, or 4 hours after, colestipol.
interactions.note: An anion-exchange resin binds anionic and other drugs non-selectively in the gut lumen, delaying or reducing absorption. Acidic drugs such as the NSAIDs bind particularly well. Solved entirely by spacing, since nothing is absorbed systemically.

interactions.suggestedAction: Keep loperamide at or below 8 mg daily. Do not exceed the label dose while on sertraline.
interactions.note: Sertraline weakly inhibits P-glycoprotein, the efflux pump that keeps loperamide out of the CNS, and weakly inhibits CYP3A4, one of its clearance routes. Neither is dramatic alone; both point the same direction.

interactions.suggestedAction: Monitor for increased sertraline side effects; a dose reduction may be appropriate.
interactions.note: Cimetidine inhibits several of sertraline's clearance routes. Reported sertraline AUC increases are around 50%, which also amplifies sertraline's own inhibitory effects on CYP2D6 — so this interaction propagates into every other sertraline pair in this database.

interactionScreening.note: Clean. Notable because sertraline plus any NSAID is a major bleeding interaction and acetaminophen is not an NSAID — this is the substitution that resolves it.
Clean. Sertraline does not meaningfully inhibit CYP1A2.
Clean on pharmacokinetic grounds, for the same reason. Additive sedation is recorded separately.
Clean or near-clean. The dramatic melatonin interaction is with fluvoxamine, a strong CYP1A2 inhibitor; sertraline is not one.
